Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of Steel 
Authority of India Limited hosted by Nuvama Wealth Management. As a reminder, all 
participants' line will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference 
call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note 
that, this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ashish Kejriwal from Nuvama Wealth Management. 
Thank you, and over to you. 
Ashish Kejriwal: 
Thank you, Iqra. Good morning, everyone. On behalf of Nuvama Wealth Management, we 
again welcome you for Q2 FY27 conference call of Steel Authority of India. We are privileged 
to have with us Dr. Ashok Panda, our Chairman and Managing Director. We also have 
Director, Commercial with us along with his team. 
 
Now, I'd request Mr. Panda for his opening remarks. And after that, we can open the floor for 
Q&A. Over to you, sir. 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Thank you very much, Mr. Ashish Kejriwal. Very good morning, everybody. I welcome all 
our investors and analysts who are joining this results con call for the financial results of SAIL 
for the quarter Q2 and H1 FY27. Before we move to the Q&A session, let me briefly run 
through the presentation on the results. 
 
Before that, let's have a look at the economic scenario, starting with the economic scenario, 
which had been prevalent during the period of the results. The resilience shown by the global 
economy has been much higher than the expectations despite effects of Middle East situation 
and trade tensions. However, as we know, there are pressures globally regarding increase in 
the Fed rate and then repo rate in our country. That is again, because of the inflationary 
pressures all over. 
 
The investment drive is being run by AI technology areas, and that is going to be the future. 
Projections have accordingly improved for calendar year 2026. The overall projections for 
calendar year 2027 are better than that of calendar year 2026, driven by growth in emerging 
and developing economies as advanced economies are expected to shrink. 
 
For Indian economy, the story has been brighter. The GDP estimates for Q1 FY27 for India 
were significantly higher than the expected numbers. Accordingly, the projections for India 
have been revised upwards by almost all major agencies. The projections are in excess of 7% 
by the agencies like IMF, World Bank, RBI, etcetera. 
 
Coming to global and Indian steel scenario, the growth factors for steel are closely linked to 
the economic performance. In fact, it is observed that the GDP growth rate bears direct 
correlation to the steel consumption. 
 
Accordingly, as on expected line, this short-range outlook, SRO published by WSA during 
October 2026 has projected a stable demand for steel in current year 2026, followed by an 
increase of almost 1.7% in calendar year 2027. 

 
 
Steel Authority of India Limited
 
 
October 28, 2026

Production and consumption continued to decline consistently in China. The current year up to 
August has already seen the production dip by around 3% in China over CPLY. Despite the 
above, China continues to dominate the world production with a share of more than 53%. 
 
SRO projects that the demand should shrink by 2% and 1% during calendar year 2026 and 
calendar year 2027, respectively, in China. Excluding China, the world is expected to see the 
steel demand grow by 1.5% and 4% in calendar year 2026 and calendar year 2027, 
respectively. 
 
Indian steel industry outshines the global counterparts in this area as well. Production in India 
during the current year up to August has shown a growth of 6% over CPLY as per WSA data. 
However, JPC data in FY26-'27, the production during H1 has grown by 3% over CPLY, 
while the consumption has got a robust growth of 8% during the same period. 
 
As per SRO, the growth in consumption is expected to be 8% for calendar year 2026 and 
calendar year 2027 as well, respectively. Meanwhile, India continues to be a net importer of 
steel during H1 FY27 and net import of around 0.6 million tons. 
 
Coming to the performance, company performance for Q2 and H1 FY26-'27. The highlights 
are as follows for Q2. Crude steel production in Q2 is 4.85 million tons with a growth of 2% 
over Q1 and 4% over Q2 last year. Sales volume of 5.2 million tons improved by 5% and 24% 
over CPLY and previous quarter, respectively. 
 
On the back of higher volumes, despite fall in realizations, sales turnover at INR31,766 crores 
in Q2 by SAIL increased by 20% over CPLY and 22% over previous quarter. As the prices of 
input, especially the imported coking coal increased during Q2, the EBITDA margins suffered. 
However, boosted by volume, as I have described already, EBITDA improved to stand at 
INR4,561 crores during Q2 of this year. 
 
Coming to PBT and PAT, PBT and PAT stood at INR2,356 crores and INR1,774 crores in Q2, 
respectively, as against INR553 crores and INR427 crores during CPLY, and INR2,159 crores 
and INR1,636 crores during quarter 1 of this year. 
 
With effective treasury management, the borrowings reduced further to INR20,583 crores as 
against INR21,729 crores as on 30th June 2026 with a reduction of INR1,146 crores in quarter 
2, and with a reduction of INR1,080 crores in H1. As a result of the debt equity ratio further 
improved to stand at 0.34x on actual basis at the end of Q2 FY26-'27. 
 
Coming to the performance of the company during H1 of FY26-'27 highlights are as follows. 
Crude steel production is at 9.6 million tons, while sales volume stood at 9.33 million tons. 
Better realizations helped the sales turnover grew by 11% over CPLY to stand at INR57,776 
crores. The production -- in the production also there is a growth of around 2% over CPLY. 
 
EBITDA, PBT and PAT figures for H1 stand at INR8,917 crores, INR4,515 crores and 
INR3,410 crores, respectively, as against INR5,754 crores, INR1,443 crores and INR1,112 
crores during CPLY registering a hefty growth -- robust growth of 55% in EBITDA, 213% in 
PBT and 207% in PAT, respectively. 

 
 
Steel Authority of India Limited

With effective treasury management, the borrowings reduced to INR20,583 crores as against 
INR21,663 crores as on 31st March with a reduction of INR1,080 crores. The finance cost has 
also come down and cost of borrowings is also at 6.34%, which is better than last year as well. 
But with the repo rate going up, probably it is going to increase in the next quarters. 
 
Going forward, quarter 3 and quarter 4 are traditionally the strongest quarter for steel industry 
and for the steel companies as well, with realizations already showing improving signs and 
actions being taken on efficiency improvement and cost reduction front, we are hopeful of 
even more robust performance during H2 '26-'27. 
 
During H1 '26-'27, other good things which happened for this company are, as I told you, 
increase in sales, reduction in inventory, increase in high-end production and dispatches and 
more importantly, almost 200% -- 167% increase in sale of iron ore fines by Steel Authority of 
India Limited. We sold around 2.5 million tons of iron ore fines in H1 as compared to 0.9 
million tons last year, and our target is around 7 million to 8 million tons for this year. And we 
are going towards that even if there are challenges going forward. So, these are the points 
which I wanted to make before we start Q&A. 
 
With these words, I hand it back to Mr. Kejriwal for opening the Q&A session, please. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. We will now begin with the question-and-answer session. The first 
question is from the line of Amit Lahoti from Aditya Birla Institutional Equities. 
Amit Lahoti: 
Good to see debt coming down in H1. Sir, my question is on the expansion plan in the FPO 
that we are planning to do. So given that the capex that we are planning would be spent over 
the next 4 to 5 years, do we really need to load equity capital upfront? Because our worry is 
that, it would put pressure on return ratios, which are already in single-digit percentage. 
 
And then it seems to have created overhang for the stock in the near term with the news of 
FPO that has come out. So can we not wait for a better time perhaps 2 years from now when 
we reach peak capex cycle to do this capital raise? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Amit. Good suggestion, point noted actually, and we are also 
on that line that even if we have planned for it, but the timing will decide when to go for that. 
Right now, it is a growth phase, and we are trying in various ways to improve profitability. So 
that is where the investor confidence is going to rejuvenate, and we'll see the appropriate time 
for the FPO. 
 
Coming to expansion plan, I have already told that actually we are on course for an expansion 
from 20 million tons to 35 million tons spread over 4 units, that is IISCO, Bokaro Steel plant, 
Bhilai and probably Rourkela, where we're looking at. So we are actively pursuing those 
things, and these are at different, different stages of tendering and in its approval stages. 
Amit Lahoti: 
Sure. And my second question is on sales volume guidance for FY27. Do we still maintain 22 
million tons?

Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Maybe around 21 million tons because in H1, we achieved 9.33 million tons. And generally, 
quarter 3 and quarter 4 become very good months in terms of production as well as sales. So 
we expect that it will be somewhere around 21 million tons. 
Amit Lahoti: 
And in this 21 million tons, does this include RINL and NMDC volumes as well? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
NMDC, we're not selling right now. As you can see in this year, we are only selling to some 
extent, RINL depending on availability from their side. Yes, some quantities is there from 
RINL as well. 
Amit Lahoti: 
So that is included in 21 million tons. 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
That is included. 
Moderator: 
The next question is from the line of Parthiv Jhonsa from Anand Rathi Shares and Stock 
Brokers. 
Parthiv Jhonsa: 
My first question is pertaining to the raw material. I believe in the last call, you had indicated 
that coal cost is expected to go down by INR1,000 in August and INR1,000 -- further 
INR1,000 in the month of September. I just wanted to know how the quarter went by and what 
is your guidance on coal cost going forward for quarter 3 and if possible, for FY27 also? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes, good question. If you look at the coal prices, quarter 1 imported coal price was 
INR21,300 per ton. And last year was how much? And in quarter 2, actually, it has increased 
to INR22,930 per ton, which is INR1,700 per ton because of the geopolitical situations and 
other demand-supply situations and the problem which happened in China because of that, 
there's the spot in the price of imported coal index. Imported coal index Platts, August index 
had gone up to $290 per ton, which has now stabilized at $266 to $267 per ton. So it kind of 
stabilized right now at the current levels. 
 
So that is the situation that the coal price is remaining on the higher side, but stable right now. 
Maybe going forward, if situation improves in China, maybe it will come down. But I think in 
quarter 3 and quarter 4, there could be a bit of reduction, but we can't exactly say that whether 
the reduction will be sharp or not because the peak rate of consumption rate of coal is going to 
come in October and November. 
 
Like as I said you in quarter 2, imported coal rate average consumption rate was INR22,930 
means INR23,000. In October, it is INR24,100, and November also, it is going to remain at the 
same level. And after that, the consumption rate will little stabilize. Maybe in quarter 3, the 
imported coal rate could be hovering around INR23,500 something. In quarter 4, it could be 
back to around INR22,000. So it will be hovering around INR22,000, INR23,000 bracket. This 
is what I guess at this point of time for imported coal rate. 
Parthiv Jhonsa: 
Okay. Sir, just continuing to that question, I believe if you see the technical parameters on one 
of the slides, I think Slide 17, the coke rate has actually gone up. So is this the overall function 
just from the pricing or also the overall productivity or the coke rate is not in your favor, which 
also might cause some issue going forward? 

 
 
Steel Authority of India Limited
 
 
October 28, 2026

Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes. All that I can say, actually this is a typical situation during the rainy season, which 
happens with the plants because the plants suffer in terms of wet coal, wet raw material and 
productivity issues with the blast furnaces. So that is over by September. And from October 
onwards, all our blast furnaces are doing good. So the technical parameters in the month of 
October have shown good improvement over Q2. 
 
So in Q3 and Q4, generally, we improve our technical parameters and we are working towards 
that to improve it further so that overall for the year, there should be better improvement in 
technical parameters. We are seized of the matter, and we are working towards that in quarter 
3 and quarter 4. 
Parthiv Jhonsa: 
Sir, my second question is on the inventory. Can you let us know what is the inventory on 
books? And out of that 21 million tons, what will be the share of inventory liquidation what 
you're expecting in the sales? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
See, as I tell you, our effort has been continuously since last year on inventory reduction and 
increasing sales and inventory reduction and reduction in borrowings. By 30th September, 
total steel inventory stands at 1.59 million tons, which includes 0.86 million tons of saleable 
steel and 0.73 million tons of in-process steel. 
 
Put together, total steel inventory is 1.5 million tons which was 1.8 million tons as on 31st 
March 2026. And it was 2.15 million tons as on 30th June 2026. So as compared to 31st 
March, there is a reduction of around 0.2 million tons in the steel inventory. And as compared 
to quarter 1, there is a reduction of around 0.55 million tons. 
 
And as of today, we are standing at 15 days of inventory, which was around 17.5 days of 
inventory as on 31st March 2026. So generally, we aim towards having around 2 weeks of 
inventory. So that is the kind of thing, and we'll try to maintain this kind of inventory. And if it 
is possible, we can reduce a little bit. Effort is still on to reduce the inventory. And because in 
quarter 3, quarter 4, the production is going to go up. So increasing sales is very important for 
us, and we are focusing on those aspects. 
Parthiv Jhonsa: 
Is it fair to assume, because you said two weeks of inventory and assuming your production go 
up slight? So, you know there's 1.59 million tons considering your saleable and in-process 
steel, can this go down to say about 1.2 million tons, 1.3 million tons or even say 1 million 
tons level, is it fair to assume? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes, something like that. We are looking at around 1.2 million tons, 1.3 million tons, it's going 
to be difficult because we have 35 stockyards and so many plant locations, they also have -- 
they have to maintain some kind of stock with them. But nonetheless, our target is actually for 
1.2 million tons, 1.3 million tons by the year-end. 
Moderator: 
The next question is from the line of Pinakin Parekh from HSBC. 
Pinakin Parekh: 
My first question is, can you give us more color on the capex ramp up? Because while we have 
been talking about a capex increase, we have not seen that flow through to numbers. So when 
do we see big projects actually seeing outflow of cash? 

 
 
Steel Authority of India Limited
 
 
October 28, 2026

Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes. capex ramp up is going to take place from this year itself. This year our guidance is for 
INR15,000 crores. Next year's guidance is in excess of INR20,000 crores. Our projects in 
IISCO Steel Plant are the ones where the cash flows are going to increase immediately. And 
that means next year the majority of the numbers will be from IISCO Steel Plant, apart from 
normal capex from other steel plants. And from the next year onwards, next to next year 
onwards it will be Bokaro followed by Bhilai Steel Plant. 
 
So next 3, 4 years, the capex is going to go up. Like this year, as I told you guidance is for 
INR15,000 crores, and H1 figure is INR5,500 crores, which is almost at the same level as the 
BE target. So Q3 and Q4 put together, the capex could be somewhere around INR9,000 crores 
to INR10,000 crores. And next year it will be in excess of INR20,000 crores, and next to next 
year it will be INR25,000 crores, like that, actually. Because in 4 years, we have to spend 
around INR1,20,000 crores on capex. 
Pinakin Parekh: 
So just to clarify you said in 4 years you have to spend INR1,20,000 crores, this is between 
FY27 to '30 or FY28 to '31? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
FY26-'27 to FY '30-'31. 
Pinakin Parekh: 
Okay. So INR1,20,000 crores which means sir that after -- so you could see the annual capex 
eventually go above INR25,000 crores in the last 2 years. It could be way above INR30,000 
crores, INR35,000 crores? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes, it is correct. 
Pinakin Parekh: 
Okay. And sir my second question is sir what is the price increases you are seeing because 
what we understand is there was spike price hikes in August September then there is some 
pullback in October. So where do prices across flats and longs stand currently versus the 
second quarter average for the company? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes. Second quarter average for the company long is INR54,400 and flat is INR57,000, 
average INR55,500 and that is situation in quarter 2. So far as October is concerned, the month 
of October, the long NSR is INR58,700, flat is INR61,700. Means around INR4,000 increase 
over Q2. And the demand is robust right now and the price levels I believe are going to 
continue. Maybe there could be some upward as well as movement because of the demand 
picking up going forward. And of course, the coal price is remaining very high. 
Pinakin Parekh: 
And sir, lastly, any guidance on employee wage cost provisions that you will start building 
from the Jan-March quarter because that is when it will start becoming due? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
We are planning for that. We have not calculated anything about it. We've started the thought 
process on this. Let's see. 
Moderator: 
The next question is from the line of Ritesh Shah from Investec. 

 
 
Steel Authority of India Limited

Ritesh Shah: 
Sir, you indicated 2.5 million tons of iron ore sales in first half. Possible for you to quantify 
how much was it in Q2? And what was the contribution at EBITDA level or the pricing at 
which we sold it? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
All I can say actually is that prices keep on varying. It's a dynamic market situation, but having 
sold around 2.5 million tons, the profit out of this is INR388 crores. And the profit out of sales 
last year, CPLY was INR124 crores. So there is incremental profit INR265 crores in this H1 
compared to last year H1. 
 
Your next question was how much was in Q2. So Q1 figure do we have. H1 figure is 2.46 
million tons. Q1 figure, I just want to find out actually. So, it could be somewhere around 1 
million ton -- 1 million ton or 1.1 million tons rough guess from my side. So, in quarter 1 also, 
we had a good sales. 
 
Quarter 2, almost kind of 1.1 million ton to 1.2 million ton would be in quarter 1. This is my 
guesswork. Because in this year, we have been focusing on it. And quarter 3, quarter 4, we are 
planning to have a major jump in sales. But we have issues with respect to that, anyway we 
were trying to tackle those issues. 
Ritesh Shah: 
Right. Sir, what is the target number for this year on iron ore sales? And sir, what are the 
issues that we are facing right now? Is it evacuation or approvals? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
The target is basically -- MOU target is 7 million tons. Our internal target was 10 million tons, 
but I believe we'll be able to achieve either 7 million or 8 million tons the way it is going on. 
There are issues not in Odisha Group of Mines, issues in Jharkhand Group of Mine because of 
on the price front as well as approval front, permit front, not approval exactly permit fronts. 
 
And we are planning to sell from Chhattisgarh Group of Mines where we've already started 
from the old mines that is Dalli-Rajhara, we are planning to see whether we can sell something 
from Rowghat mines. Major chunk is going to come from the new mines which is Rowghat. 
So because it is a new operating mine, so there are down level challenges, but we are trying to 
tackle those. 
Ritesh Shah: 
Right. And sir, just last question. In the notes to accounts, you have indicated we are looking to 
also utilize low-grade iron ore and put on certain plants to process it. Sir, is it possible to 
process this low-grade ore if it is 48%, 50% FE? Do we have the technology for that? And if 
we have the technology for it, how much will be the costing be it versus the current costing for 
normal open cast iron ore mining? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
So low-grade iron ore, which are available in all the mines. Let me take you mines wise. In 
Chhattisgarh Group of Mines, we have low-grade iron ore, which is getting beneficiated there 
itself. That is called silica reduction plant and SBP beneficiation plant. So already, they've 
been doing it and we'll increase that quantity. 
 
Coming to Odisha Group of Mines and Jharkhand Group of Mines, we have low-grade iron 
ore mines in terms of SGF dump as well as tailings. Much of this we are trying to sell actually.

Right now, we have other issues like government-related issues and pricing-related issues. 
We're trying to have a breakthrough in that after which we'll be selling. 
 
Even from Odisha Group of Mines, we are selling some tailings over there. So it is a hybrid 
mode. In certain cases, we are beneficiating and consuming. In certain other cases, we are 
selling it outright. But going forward, in future, we'll have beneficiation plants, which will be 
coming up at Gua mines in future so that much of the subgrade mines can be beneficiated at 
Gua mines and then pelletized and pellets can be consumed. So, these are our future plans. 
Moderator: 
The next question is from the line of Shivkumar Prajapati from Mirae Asset. 
Shivkumar Prajapati: 
My first question is on Tasra coking coal mines. So, are we on track to start this mines by Q4 
FY27? And by when can we see the savings reflecting in our numbers? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes. Thank you for this question. This is what we are also looking at and Tasra is on track, and 
it is going to start -- is going to start production from January 2027 itself. That means in 
quarter 4, we'll be able to take the profit benefit out of that. So that is going to give us a lot of 
savings in terms of cost of ores. 
Shivkumar Prajapati: 
Okay. And sir, my next question is on iron ore mines, basically Rowghat mines where our EC 
for 6 MTPA is due, I mean it is remaining. So by when it is expected to come? And next on 
this Gua Ore Mines where we have plans to expand it by 2.5x, I mean, basically taking the 
capacity up to 10 MTPA. If you could help us with the time lines? And third one on this is our 
2 MTPA pellet plant at RSP, is it on track? 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Yes. Let me answer your questions one by one. You started about iron ore mines in Rowghat. 
The MDO has already started working over there. Right now, they are doing the interim 
mining. And in the interim mining we have taken EC clearance of, I believe, 3 million tons, 
and we are almost hitting those levels. 
 
But going forward, when the main mining is going to start by the MDO, which will take 
maybe another 1 year or more than 1 year, then the ramp-up is going to start. 3 million tons by 
-- I mean, right now, 3 million tons after that, ultimately, it will go towards 14 million tons in 
3, 4 years' time. So it will go in a phased manner. 
 
Right now, 2 million tons and after that, it's going to be 3 million tons, then 4 million tons, 
then 6 million tons, then 9 million tons, then 14 million tons. So this is the kind of trajectory 
on which it will be traveling. So as of now, things are on track, and we are critically 
monitoring the progress at Rowghat iron ore mines. That is about Rowghat. 
 
Regarding Gua, we have a plan to increase the production from 4 million tons to 10 million 
tons by appointing an MDO. So that is going to take a little more time because of the clearance 
and other things. Regarding the pellet plant RSP, which is 2 million tons per annum, that is on 
course and it is going to start as per the set target lines. It is in the advanced stages. 
Shivkumar Prajapati: 
Okay. Sir, one last question. Our aspiration is to reach 100 MTPA of iron ore production by 
FY '30, FY '31. Last year, we did around 38, 39 MTPA, and H1 of this year, we are close to

19, 20 MTPA. So what is our guidance here for FY27? And if you can help me understand the 
bridge between our current 40 MTPA versus 100 MTP of aspiration? And does this also 
include any contribution from Chiria mines. 
Ashok Kumar Panda: 
Let me answer this question. Actually, last year, we achieved around 38 million tons is that 
correct. This year, our target itself is 56 million tons, but I think we'll be achieving somewhere 
around 48 million to 50 million tons. And H1, as you said, is 19.5 million is around 20 million 
tons. H1 is 20 million means in the dry season, it will be much more than 20 million tons. So 
that is why I told probably we go towards 48 million tons or 50 million tons on the optimistic 
lines. So that is going to happen. 
 
And regarding 100 million tons, that is an ambitious target by us for '30-'31 or '31-'32. It a lot 
depends on Rowghat, lot depends on Gua. And of course, we are going to start increasing our 
production from Bolani in Odisha and Kalta from Odisha and Taldih is going to come on 
course. So with all these things, we are expecting 100 million tons, which is an ambitious 
target. 
 
But if not 100 million tons, then at least we'll able to achieve 80 million tons, 85 million tons 
something like that because as I told you clearly, one is Rowghat, the other one is Bolani, 
Kalta, Taldih. Taldih already MDO is working over there. And then another one is Gua here. 
 
And while considering 100 million tons, it doesn't consider anything from Chiria. Chiria is in a 
different state altogether, clearances and other problems are there in that. So, it doesn't include 
Chiria. Without including Chiria, we have a plan -- ambitious plan of 100 million tons by '30-
'31 or '31-'32. 
Moderator: 
The next question is from the line of Vikash Singh from ICICI Securities Limited. 
Vikash Singh: 
Sir, just wanted to understand that you said that you would have to spend INR1 lakh crores in 
capex in the 4 years. If I remember our previous stance was that we will go into the capex on a 
stepwise basis so that the overall debt should not inflate. Sir, just 2 questions related to this. 
 
Firstly, in terms of this INR1 lakh crores, which are the plants where we have the full land 
available free of any encroachment, and the capex for particularly those plants, how much that 
would be? And secondly, that what happened to the step down, what kind of the debt -- 
incremental debt addition you could see from this? 
Ashok Kumar Panda:
